newsitem.title: FRANCE: Casino shares rise on chairman's remarks.
newsitem.headline: Casino shares rise on chairman's remarks.

text.p: Shares in retailer Casino rallied on Monday after its chairman rekindled merger speculation by telling a newspaper it was important to build a second French food retailer with annual sales of around 200 billion francs, in addition to leader Carrefour.
Asked about a possible and much-rumoured linkup between Casino and Promodes, Casino chairman Georges Plassat told the newspaper Les Echos that anything was possible.
His remarks, following similarly ambiguous comments from leading Casino shareholder Jean-Charles Naouri, boosted the stock. It was up 3.03 percent at 265.30 francs at 1215 GMT.
The market in the meantime was flat.
Some brokers said the stock was also benefiting from brokerage DB Bourse's move on Friday to raise its recommendation to accumulate from hold.

Plassat said it was "absolutely imperative" for a successful retail group to develop internationally from a strong domestic position. "We need to build another French group with 200 billion francs in sales," he said.
The figure, more than triple Casino's 1996 sales of 66.84 billion francs, caught the market's attention.
"Previously, they said they would be fine with 100 billion francs of sales, but now they think 200 billion is needed," one portfolio manager said.
Market operators said the stock's gain could be short-lived as Promodes does not seem keen on an alliance in the immediate future.
One fund manager said the group was talking up its stock price. "If they want to get married, they should get married. They don't have to go through the press," he said.
Another said Casino was asking too high a price.
Promodes has said it would be careful to ensure that its profitability was not undermined by any acquisition.
